description: We are Team NRS (Nova Rover Systems), a passionate group of developers and space enthusiasts specializing in AI and software engineering. Our mission is to bridge the gap between complex NASA data and the public through Citizen Science. We build interactive, AI-driven tools to make space exploration accessible, accurate, and engaging for everyone.
summary:
**Planet X and SPHEREx** is an interactive web platform designed to make NASA’s massive infrared space archives accessible, visual, and engaging for everyone.

### What We Built

We created a dual-interface web application consisting of an immersive 3D cinematic storytelling landing page and an advanced **Sky Explorer dashboard**. The platform features instant coordinate lookup, pre-tested celestial target presets, an automated guided tour, and real-time infrared spectral band visualization.

### The Problem It Addresses

NASA space telescopes—such as SPHEREx, WISE, and Euclid—generate vast, petabyte-scale data about the infrared universe. However, this raw data is traditionally locked behind complex technical barriers, making it slow and difficult for students, educators, and citizen scientists to explore, query, or analyze without heavy network latency.

### How It Helps and Why It Matters

Our platform solves this by using optimized spatial indexing ("Sky Zoning") and a **Difference Mode** that subtracts background starlight across multiple time epochs. This allows users to instantly "time-travel" across the infrared sky, strip away static background stars, and effortlessly spot moving or flaring cosmic anomalies (like variable stars, comets, or outer-system bodies) in milliseconds.

By turning complex astrophysical telemetry into an intuitive, browser-based exploration tool, our project democratizes space data, empowers classrooms, and inspires the next generation .
details:
Project Technical Explanation & Submission Dossier

Project Name: Planet X and SPHEREx

Team Name: Nova Rover Systems

Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge (Cairo 2026)

1. Executive Summary & Core Mission

Planet X and SPHEREx is an advanced, dual-interface astronomical exploration platform engineered to democratize access to NASA’s petabyte-scale infrared archives. By bridging the gap between raw, complex astronomical telemetry and intuitive interactive exploration, our application empowers citizen scientists, educators, and researchers to time-travel across the infrared cosmos, track transient cosmic objects, and analyze stellar spectra with unprecedented ease and precision.

Main Use Case (Cairo Submission Focus)

The primary operational use case of our platform is the rapid isolation and multi-epoch spectral analysis of astronomical transients and moving targets (such as high-proper-motion brown dwarfs, distant comets, variable stars, and hypothetical outer-solar-system bodies like Planet X). Using pre-tested celestial patches (e.g., Andromeda, the Galactic Center, Orion Nebula, and WISE 0855), users can instantly query coordinate zones, compare baseline epochs, and detect shifting or flaring anomalies without suffering the massive latency typically associated with querying raw all-sky astronomical databases.

2. Technical Architecture & How It Works

Our architecture is built around three core pillars designed to handle massive data volumes efficiently:

  • Spatial Partitioning & Sky Zoning: To eliminate network and rendering latency, the celestial sphere is partitioned into indexed Sky Zones. Instead of streaming massive all-sky maps simultaneously, the application focuses client-side rendering on optimized, pre-tested high-interest target patches where astronomical targets are pre-validated.
    • Single Mode: Renders direct observational flux frames at specific epochs, allowing users to study baseline static sky brightness and morphology.
    • Difference Mode: Executes differential image processing by subtracting the multi-epoch mean background. This instantly strips away static background stars and highlights moving or transient sources.
  • Spectral Band Analysis: The platform maps out 102 infrared spectral bands across detectors D1 through D6 (modeled after the SPHEREx instrument framework), enabling users to inspect flux-versus-wavelength curves and identify ice absorption features, galactic structures, and stellar classifications.

3. How NASA Data Supports the Solution

Our platform is directly anchored in NASA’s premier astrophysics missions:

  • SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer): Provides the foundational framework for our 102-band near-infrared spectral processing and cosmological ice-mapping storytelling.
  • WISE, NEOWISE, and Euclid Archives: Utilized for multi-epoch temporal comparison baselines, supplying the historical sky coverage required for differential time-series analysis.

This data is integrated into our spatial indexing pipeline, transforming raw fits and catalog data into smooth, client-side interactive visual frames and flux graphs.

4. Tools, Languages, Software, and Hardware

  • Frontend & User Interface: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Tailwind CSS for responsive, high-performance styling.
  • 3D Graphics & Animation: Three.js (for immersive space rendering and starfield visualization), GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform) with ScrollTrigger, and Lenis for cinematic smooth scrolling.
  • Backend & Data Processing Utilities: Python (leveraging pandas and openpyxl for background data pipelining, astronomical catalog formatting, and roster management).
  • Deployment & Hosting: Git/GitHub for version control; Firebase Hosting for global, low-latency production deployment.
  • Development Environment: Windows development workstations running Visual Studio Code.

5. Benefits, Impact, and Long-Term Goals

  • Democratization of Science: Lowers the barrier to entry for space data, turning complex infrared spectroscopy into an accessible, engaging web experience.
  • Educational Empowerment: Serves as an interactive virtual observatory for classrooms and universities to teach observational astronomy and data science.
  • Citizen Science Acceleration: Provides tools that can scale to assist amateur astronomers in flagging real sky anomalies.

6. Current Working Features vs. Future Roadmap

To assist judges inspecting the delivered static and hosted project without a live walkthrough, features are strictly categorized below:

🟢 Fully Working & Verified Features (Delivered in Current Prototype)

  • Cinematic 3D Landing Page (index.html): Fully interactive Three.js space narrative comparing legacy missions with SPHEREx.
  • Advanced Sky Explorer Dashboard (explorer.html): Fully operational query interface supporting coordinate input (RA/Dec) and pre-tested celestial presets.
  • Automated Guided Tour: An interactive, step-by-step onboarding walkthrough that triggers automatically upon entering the explorer.
  • Mode Switching & Temporal Scrubbing: Functional UI toggles for Single vs. Difference mode and frame playback controls.
  • Spectral Plotting Simulation: Dynamic visualization of infrared spectral bands across detectors D1–D6.

🔵 Future Roadmap (Post-Hackathon Expansion)

  • Live NASA API Integration: Transitioning from optimized pre-tested local data patches to live, streaming queries against NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive REST endpoints.
  • Advanced Machine Learning Classification: Integrating automated anomaly detection models to flag genuine transient candidates in real-time.

7. System Limitations

  • Client-Side Processing Bounds: To maintain high frame rates and zero-latency interaction in a browser environment, the current prototype relies on pre-tested, high-density target patches rather than querying raw petabyte-scale all-sky FITS files directly on the client.
  • Simulated Telemetry vs. Live Stream: While scientific math, spectral band distributions, and differential processing logic strictly reflect authentic mission parameters, live real-time telemetry streaming from active orbital observatories is reserved for the production roadmap phase.
